title: A Systematic Literature Review on Personal Financial Management Practices: Budgeting, Investment, Debt, and Saving
authors: Elliyana, E.; Maricar, R.; Toalib, R.
venue: World Journal of Economics, Business and Management
tldr: Synthesizes 47 studies on PFM finding financial literacy as pivotal for saving, investment, and debt management, with digital tools as significant enablers despite behavioral challenges.
problem_and_motivation: PFM practices directly influence financial well-being, but behavioral and social factors continue to challenge the efficacy of financial education and digital tool adoption.
approach: Systematic literature review of 47 peer-reviewed studies published 2018-2024.
Synthesizes findings across multiple countries on budgeting, investment, debt, and saving.
Analyzes financial literacy, digital tools, and behavioral/social factor roles.
findings: Financial literacy enhances saving habits, responsible investment, and effective debt management.
Digital financial tools enable financial discipline especially among youth and urban consumers.
Behavioral factors like peer influence, impulsivity, and media exposure challenge financial education.

definitions.definition: Personal Financial Management encompassing budgeting, saving, investing, and debt handling.

citations.author: None
citations.claim: Systematic review; citations too numerous to list individually.

topics.name: Financial Behavior of Filipino Young Professionals

topics.name: Budgeting Strategies as Domain Knowledge
topics.justification: Core focus on budgeting practices synthesized from 47 studies.

topics.name: Savings Goal Management in PFMS
topics.justification: Reviews saving practices and determinants extensively.

topics.name: Debt Management in PFMS

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Consolidates diverse PFM literature into a multidimensional framework showing interplay of socioeconomic, psychological, technological, and institutional factors. Demonstrates digital tools complement but cannot replace financial literacy.
directly_justifies: Financial literacy enhances saving habits and debt management.
Digital financial tools enable financial discipline among youth.
limits: Review covers international studies, not specifically Philippine context.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 domains. Flagged 7.A, 13.A, 13.B (high), 1.C (medium). Rejected algorithmic topics as this is a literature review.

limitations: Geographic coverage not exhaustive for Philippine-specific PFM research.
remember_this: Financial literacy is pivotal for all PFM dimensions.
Digital tools enable financial discipline among youth.
Behavioral factors challenge financial education efficacy.
